brief: A crowded underground platform is seen as a train arrives. Commuters are rendered as hyperreal faces that smear and repeat across the frame in stuttering staggered echoes, each step slightly offset and fading, like step-printed film. One woman in a mustard raincoat stays sharp at the centre, every eyelash and button in focus. Around her, figures dissolve into horizontal trails of charcoal and soft pastel-like smudge. The fluorescent light is greenish-white, with tiled walls in cream and ox-blood trim. Strong lateral motion streaks drive across the composition, which feels restless, urban and dreamlike.

A long, thin panoramic band of desert highway, the horizon pushed into the lower third. A chrome fuel tanker approaches from the vanishing point, and above it hangs its own inverted, stretched double, sheared into wobbling horizontal slices by heat. Soft airbrushed spray builds the bleached cerulean-to-bone sky gradient and the shimmering haze. Crisp graphite and fine pen give the hyperreal detail of the grille, the rivets and the asphalt cracks in the near foreground. Edges sharpen toward the viewer and dissolve into trembling, smeared bands at distance. It feels like heat you can see, a photograph that refuses to hold still.

A tight portrait of a road worker's shoulders and chin under flat overcast daylight. The fluorescent yellow-green hi-vis vest and orange hard hat dominate the frame. The palette is pure road-sign enamel: safety yellow, signal orange, retroreflective silver and asphalt grey. Flat, dense marker covers the vest. Fine sprayed sparkle and pen dots render the glass-bead tape, so it glitters like a sign caught in headlights. Stubble, sweat and scuffed fabric are drawn with hyperreal attention. The composition is bold, central-cropped and blunt, as legible from a distance as a highway warning.

A spent marathon runner at the finish, wrapped in a crinkled thermal blanket, shown in close half-length. Their salt-streaked face is drawn in fine sepia and umber pencil with photographic pores and sweat. The foil cape dominates the image. It is broken into sharp polygonal crease facets, each filled with flat marker gradients that shift abruptly from silver to violet, cyan, lime and copper. Prismatic rainbow bands slice diagonally across the folds. The reflections of the crowd are warped and smeared within the facets. The mood is exhausted triumph under harsh midday light.

A chrome-and-bakelite toaster on a kitchen counter at early morning, rendered photographically but in a mid-century picture-book palette: mustard, avocado, dusty teal, tomato red and warm cream only. Two slices pop halfway up. Every crumb on the speckled laminate is described individually. Flat opaque colour areas carry a dry crayon tooth that lets paper grain show. The reflection in the chrome warps a stylised kitchen window into soft bands. The composition is off-centre and low, with the toaster pushed to the left edge and a generous sweep of counter.

A snow squall erases almost everything. The page is a sheet of soft grey-white spray and windblown pencil flecks driving diagonally. Emerging only partly from it is a fire hydrant buried to its shoulders. The cap and one bolted nozzle are rendered with obsessive clarity in cadmium red marker, ice rime clinging in crisp white pencil. Toward the edges every detail dissolves into white, and the drifting snow is laid in as layered translucent wash. The piece feels cold, disoriented and quiet, a single coloured certainty inside the blankness.

The corner of an empty concrete parking garage at mid-afternoon. A single orange traffic cone stands where a slab of sunlight meets a hard diagonal shadow. Lay the composition out as razor-edged flat fields of marker: warm putty grey, cool slate shadow, a stripe of chrome yellow paint line and the cone's vivid safety orange. Not one edge is softened. Inside each field, a faint fine spray of grit, pencil-drawn hairline cracks and oil-stain mottling supply the photographic truth. The cone's reflective collar is the only glint. The mood is silent, architectural and clinical, like a Kelly canvas that turns out to be a photograph.

A stacked woodpile beneath an oak, painted like a Barbizon plein-air study pushed to hyperreal intensity at its heart. The central split logs get microscopic attention: growth rings, splinters, lichen crusts and bark ridges in fine pencil over wet watercolour. Toward the edges the image loosens into broad puddled washes of raw umber, sap green and grey-violet, with charcoal-like scrubbed shadow and quick unfinished brush scribbles. Dappled afternoon light falls in warm ochre patches. The sense is of an outdoor painter who became obsessed with one log, letting the meadow dissolve around it.

Extreme hyperreal close-up of a striped toothpaste ribbon extruded onto toothbrush bristles. The paste is rendered like wedding-cake piping: thick, raised, ridged lines of opaque marker in mint, pearl white and candy pink. Each one has a rounded bead edge and a soft cast shadow, coiling in perfect scallops. The translucent blue bristles fan beneath it in fine parallel pen strokes with glinting tips. The background is a sugary powder-blue gradient laid in with soft spray. Everything feels confectionery, overly clean and delicately ornamental: the morning routine treated as a tiered celebration cake.

A cracked-open purple sea urchin on a bed of crushed ice, its five coral-orange roe lobes glistening. Build the whole image as Byzantine mosaic: a field of small square and wedge tesserae, each a single dab of flat marker. Use lapis, garnet, aubergine and tangerine smalti, with flecks of gold leaf in the ice highlights. Each tessera sits slightly askew in thin graphite grout lines. Rows follow the contours of the spines like the haloes of saints. From afar it reads as a photograph. Close up, it becomes glittering, devotional, fragmented stone, set against a deep cobalt ground.

A coil of rusted barbed wire strung across a pale winter sky, every twist and barb in sharp focus. Execute it as a drypoint: monochrome warm black on cream. Draw scratched pen lines with a soft, fuzzy burr along one side, so the darkest strokes bloom velvety while the thin ones stay wiry. A faint wiped plate tone, smudged like charcoal haze, sits behind, heavier at the corners. Rust is suggested only by tight cross-hatching and stippled pits. Frost crystals on the barbs are tiny reserved specks of bare paper. The image is austere and tactile, as if scored into copper by a patient, cold hand.

Looking down into a stainless steel stand-mixer bowl just as the paddle starts. A spiralling plume of flour lifts into the air like a small dust devil. Render the vortex in curving flow-field pencil arcs that tighten toward the centre, veiled by layers of soft beige and ivory spray. Escaping particles drift out as stippled specks. The brushed-steel bowl reflects the plume in warped, cool grey streaks. Cracked eggshells and a butter wrapper sit at the rim in sharp detail. The palette is wheat, bone and steel. The motion feels caught mid-whirl: chaotic at the core, serene at the edges.

A close, tilted view into the bowl of a chromed steelpan. Its hammered note-dimples each reflect a sky of electric violet, molten gold and deep teal. Two drumsticks with worn rubber tips rest across the rim. Build the metal in airbrushed spray gradients, layering iridescent hues so each dimple reads as its own small, glowing world. Fine metallic pen traces the seams and tool marks. Tiny bright starburst highlights sit on the rims. The palette is magenta-to-indigo, ultramarine, burnished bronze and gold. It feels celebratory, cosmic and rhythmic: carnival metal as a portal.

A strict bird's-eye view straight down onto a courtyard fountain basin, composed as a fourfold garden plan. Four narrow stone water channels meet at a central octagonal pool. Each quadrant holds a different hyperreal surface: wet turquoise zellige tile, dry terracotta gravel, a fallen fig leaf, and rippling water catching sky. Fine pen linework defines the geometry with mapmaker precision. Layered watercolour glazes in lapis, verdigris and sandstone pink carry the water's caustic light and each tile's glaze crazing. The composition is perfectly symmetrical and calm, with tiny real disorder breaking the order.

A hyperreal black Bakelite rotary telephone, cropped to its dial and a looping coiled cord. It is placed on a Bauhaus poster ground of flat primary marker shapes: a cadmium red circle behind the dial, a chrome yellow diagonal band, a cobalt square and a thick black bar. The geometry is crisp and asymmetric, with no text. The telephone itself is rendered photographically in graphite and black marker: glossy reflections, worn finger-holes, the chrome finger-stop gleaming. The coiled cord casts a sharp shadow across the coloured planes. The mood is rational and graphic, with a nostalgic hum.

A hyperreal sandcastle on a beach seen from a high oblique bird's-eye view, laid out like a pictorial tourist map. A dotted trail of footprints winds between landmarks: a moat with trapped seawater, a stranded crab, a red plastic spade, a half-buried flip-flop and a crumpled ice-cream wrapper. Each object is rendered photographically in fine pen and watercolour. The sand is cheerful flat washes of buff and apricot, the tide edge a frilled band of turquoise and foam white. A small decorative compass rose sits in one corner. The mood is breezy, souvenir-like and playful, yet minutely observed.

A dark, wet slate patio at dawn, crossed by the glistening trails of garden snails. Two hyperreal snails sit mid-composition, their mottled amber shells and moist grey bodies in exquisite detail. The trails behave like cloud-chamber tracks. They are thin silvery filaments in fine pen that branch, curl into tight spirals, overlap and fade, each catching iridescent hints of violet and pale green. The slate is a deep charcoal mass with subtle pencil-drawn layering. The atmosphere is scientific and quiet: a record of invisible journeys, rendered as luminous wiry lines on near-black.

A steamed hairy crab on a pale celadon dish, painted in the manner of gongbi. Even, unbroken iron-wire outlines in fine dark pen define every leg joint, bristle and shell ridge. Colour builds up in many thin, patient watercolour layers of vermilion, cinnabar and persimmon orange. The carapace glows with a soft gradient, and droplets of condensation gather on the plate. A small dish of vinegar with ginger slivers sits to one side. The ground is warm, aged silk-beige with faint washed texture. The composition is asymmetric and airy. The effect is refined, scholarly and appetising.

A tight, edge-to-edge crop of a gift basket of navel oranges sealed in crinkled cellophane, knotted with a curling magenta ribbon. The fruit reads through the plastic in saturated cadmium orange marker. The cellophane exists only as overlapping transparent veils, prismatic slivers of pale cyan and lilac, and hard white fracture-highlights drawn in crisp pen along every crease. Where folds stack, colours deepen and shift, as if seen through layered tinted film. Wicker peeks at the bottom in warm ochre hatching. The effect is glittering, noisy, a little garish: the specular chaos of plastic wrap rendered with obsessive precision.

A fully inflated pufferfish, rendered with hyperreal spines and wet, glassy eyes. Its body is built like reverse appliqué: stacked contour channels cut through layers of colour. Each concentric band follows the swell of the fish in flat marker, alternating scarlet, tangerine, black and emerald. Narrow slits reveal lower layers, and every band edge carries a slightly uneven, hand-cut wobble. Inside that graphic structure, each spine is realistically modelled with pencil shading and a pinpoint highlight. The ground is a deep indigo field filled with tiny repeated slit-channels. The piece reads as dense, festive and textile-like, yet unnervingly lifelike up close.
